evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: securelist.com Updated Apr 15th, 2015 The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT: the Empire Strikes Back One of the most active APT groups in Asia, and especially around the South China Sea area is "Naikon".

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: The name Naikon comes from a custom user agent string, "NOKIAN95/WEB", located within the backdoor:

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: NOKIAN string in Naikon backdoor The Naikon group is mostly active in countries such as the Philippines, Malaysia, Cambodia, Indonesia, Vietnam, Myanmar, Singapore, and Nepal, hitting a variety of targets in a very opportunistic way.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: National Police Presidential Management Staff The Naikon group used mostly spear­phished documents for the attacks, with CVE­2012­0158 exploits that dropped the group's signature backdoor.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: The backdoor connects to the command server located at philippinenews[.]mooo[.]com .

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Victims of Hellsing attacks The actor targets its intended victims using spear­phishing emails with archives containing malware, similar to the one it used against the Naikon group.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: We've observed RAR, ZIP and 7ZIP archives in the attacks ­ the 7ZIP archives with passwords were probably introduced as a way to bypass the recent security features on Gmail, which block password­ protected archives with executables inside.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Artifacts and overlap with other APTs Interestingly, some of the infrastructure used by the attackers appears to overlap (although around a year apart) with a group tracked internally at Kaspersky Lab as PlayfullDragon (also known as "GREF"); while other aspects of the infrastructure overlap with a group known as Mirage or Vixen Panda.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Another overlap we observed is with an APT known as Cycldek or Goblin Panda.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: It appears that the Hellsing developer started with the Cycldek sources and worked together with the operators from other APT groups.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: One can see the project name is Hellsing and the malware is called "msger":

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: The Hellsing series chronicles the efforts of the mysterious and secret Hellsing Organization, as it combats vampires , ghouls , and other supernatural foes; which makes it perhaps an appropriate name for our group.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: In addition to the Hellsing/msger malware, we've identified a second generation of Trojan samples which appear to be called "xweber" by the attackers: "Xweber" seems to be the more recent Trojan, taking into account compilation timestamps.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: The "Xweber" samples are from 2013 and from 2014, indicating that at some point during 2013 the "msger" malware project was renamed and/or integrated into "Xweber".

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: During our investigation we've observed the Hellsing APT using both the "Xweber" and "msger" backdoors in their attacks, as well as other tools named "xrat", "clare", "irene" and "xKat".

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: One such tool is "test.exe":

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: g g g Name test.exe Size 45,568 bytes Type Win32 PE i386 executable This tool is used to gather information and test available proxies.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Another attack tool deployed in a victim's environment was a file system driver, named "diskfilter.sys", although internally it claims to be named "xrat.sys".

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Name xkat.exe Size 78,848 bytes Type Win32 PE i386 executable This is a powerful file deletion and process killer which uses a driver (Dbgv.sys) to perform the operations.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Conclusions The Hellsing APT group is currently active in the APAC region, hitting targets mainly in the South China Sea area, with a focus on Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: The group has a relatively small footprint compared to massive operations such as " Equation ".

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: The targeting of the Naikon group by the Hellsing APT is perhaps the most interesting part.

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: So, where does the Hellsing name come from? One of the samples we analysed (md5: 036e021e1b7f61cddfd294f791de7ea2) appears to have been compiled in a rush and the attacker forgot to remove the debug information. One can see the project name is Hellsing and the malware is called "msger":

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Once the Hellsing attackers compromise a computer, they deploy other tools which can be used for gathering further information about the victim or doing lateral movement. One such tool is "test.exe":

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Name test.exe

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Another attack tool deployed in a victim's environment was a file system driver, named "diskfilter.sys", although internally it claims to be named "xrat.sys". The driver is unsigned and compiled for 32­bit Windows. It was used briefly in 2013, before being abandoned by the attackers, possibly due to Windows 7 driver signing requirements:

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist
evidences.text: Name xkat.exe

evidences.report_id: The Chronicles of the Hellsing APT_ the Empire Strikes Back - Securelist

evidences.text: This is a powerful file deletion and process killer which uses a driver (Dbgv.sys) to perform the operations. We've seen it being used by the attackers to kill and delete malware belonging to their competitors.
